backlog.spec: Replace the CatBoost residual model with LightGBM in DART mode (boosting_type='dart', objective='l1', drop_rate=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, about 400 rounds, learning_rate 0.05, num_leaves 15, feature_fraction 0.5, bagging_fraction 0.8 with bagging_freq 1). Fit it on the same OLS-prior residual target and use the seed as random_state. DART's tree dropout is a different regulariser from CatBoost's, and it targets the overfitting on rare fingerprint bits that the family-swap trials did not address.
backlog.title: DART-style LightGBM L1 residual model

backlog.spec: After the OLS prior, fit a sklearn RandomForestRegressor (300 trees, min_samples_leaf=3, max_features=0.3, random_state=seed) on the residual using featurize() columns. At prediction time, do not use the forest mean: for each test molecule, collect the training residuals that share a leaf with it across all trees, weight each by 1/(leaf size) summed over trees, and take the weighted median as the residual prediction. This gives a conditional-median estimate matched to the MAE metric. Implement with apply() on train and test, and keep it vectorised.
backlog.title: Quantile regression forest conditional median on the residual

backlog.spec: Replace the four-term OLS prior with a small symbolic-regression prior. Using only the four base features (TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors, MolLogP) plus their squares and pairwise products, run a numpy genetic search over formulas of depth at most 3 (operators +, -, *, and a protected divide). Population 200, 40 generations, tournament selection, subtree crossover and mutation, with fitness equal to the training MAE plus a size penalty of 0.002 per node. Use the seed for all random draws, keep the best formula, and fit its linear coefficients by least squares. CatBoost MAE then fits the residual as before. This is a bold architecture change to the prior, not a new feature block.
backlog.title: Genetic-programming symbolic prior

backlog.spec: Append a compact histogram of topological distances between heteroatom pairs (N, O, F, Cl, S, P, Br), computed with Chem.GetDistanceMatrix on each molecule. Count pairs for distances 1 to 12 with distances above 12 pooled into one bin, separately for pair classes N-N, N-O, O-O, and hetero-to-carbon, giving about 48 integer columns. Fit no transform, use float32, and concatenate with the existing featurize() output. Heteroatom spacing is the topology that drives hydrogen-bond and polarity effects in permeability, and it is not in Morgan counts or the RDKit descriptor list.
backlog.title: Heteroatom topological-distance pair histogram

backlog.spec: Replace the CatBoost residual model with componentwise L1 gradient boosting. On the OLS residual, run 300 steps. At each step, for every standardised RDKit descriptor column, fit a one-dimensional cubic-spline base learner (about 5 knots at training quantiles) by least squares to the sign of the current residual, then choose the column that most reduces the training MAE and add a 0.1-shrunk step. Store the chosen column and coefficients. Predict by summing the stored steps. Fingerprint columns are excluded, which makes this a sparse additive model. Use the seed to break ties and to subsample columns each step.
backlog.title: Componentwise L1 boosting with spline base learners

backlog.spec: Keep the OLS prior and the CatBoost MAE residual fit. Add a second CatBoost model with loss_function='Poisson' on the OLS residual shifted to be nonnegative (residual minus its training minimum, plus 1e-3), with the same depth, learning rate and iteration count. Invert the shift at prediction time by subtracting the training minimum that was added. Average the two residual predictions with equal weight. A count-type likelihood fits the upper tail differently from the MAE model, so the blend may cover the tails that a median-only fit leaves out.
backlog.title: Poisson-shifted residual model blended with the MAE model

backlog.spec: In featurize(), replace the raw Morgan count values with log1p(count) and then divide each molecule's fingerprint row by its L2 norm (zero rows stay zero). Leave the RDKit descriptor columns unchanged. This keeps the count information from the 2048-bin radius-2 block but limits the leverage of heavily repeated substructures such as aromatic CH, which the count variant in an earlier slot may have over-weighted. The change is one line in the fingerprint loop and needs no new dependencies.
backlog.title: Log1p count transform with L2-normalised fingerprint rows

backlog.spec: Before the final fit, run one extra CatBoost MAE fit on the OLS residual with the training targets permuted within the training set (seed-controlled permutation). Measure the mean absolute value of its test-fold predictions as a null noise level, then shrink the real residual prediction by a factor equal to max(0, 1 - null_level / real_level), where real_level is the mean absolute residual prediction of the real model on the same training rows. This is a bold, label-free calibration of how much of the boosted correction is memorised noise. It adds one extra fit per job and leaves the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Shuffled-target label-noise calibration of the residual shrink

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, draw 7 bootstrap samples of the training rows, grouping rows by Murcko scaffold so that each bootstrap resamples whole scaffolds, not single molecules. For each resample, fit the OLS prior and the CatBoost MAE residual model with a different seed derived from the job seed. Predict the test molecules with each of the 7 pipelines and return the element-wise median of their predictions. Scaffold-level resampling matches the grouped evaluation, and the median is a robust combination for MAE. The idea differs from the earlier random-subspace and depth-bag attempts because the resampling unit is the scaffold, not the feature set or the tree depth.
backlog.title: Inner-scaffold seed bagging with median aggregation of CatBoost residuals

incumbent.description: Fit an OLS baseline on TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors and MolLogP, train the existing CatBoost model on the residuals, and add the linear prediction back for test molecules (applied to the current CatBoost incumbent, since the spec's random forest is no longer in train.py).

memo: Helped: compact features (MACCS 0.4096 vs 0.4417 baseline), CatBoost MAE loss (0.3837), and an OLS prior on TPSA/MolWt/NumHDonors/MolLogP with CatBoost fit on the residual (0.3757, 0.3664; incumbent mean 0.3711). Since then nearly all of about 70 slots were rejected, mostly within noise (sd about 0.0037). Near-misses: Abraham six-term prior 0.3685 (unreplicated), CatBoost RMSE residual 0.3685, two-model averaging 0.3687, two-phase Huber 0.3701, EState 0.3708. Did not help: family swaps (LightGBM 0.3882, MLP 0.4734, Tanimoto kernel ridge 0.4357), extra feature blocks (torsion 0.3771, 3D shape 0.3780, Gobbi 0.3831, BRICS 0.3805), target tricks (winsorising 0.3752, smoothing 0.3845), fancier priors (local linear 0.3886, Nystroem 0.3915, ARD 0.3876), and regularization tweaks. Next: replicate the Abraham prior and RMSE residual, then combine them, with seed averaging. Then tune CatBoost depth, learning rate, iterations and l2 on the residual setup. Avoid new family swaps, feature blocks and priors.
